whisper_prompt: Mathematics. Hilbert's Hotel. Infinity. Countable infinity. Bijection. Natural numbers. Infinite bus.

sections.title: A HOTEL THAT IS ALWAYS FULL
animations: Introduce an extra guest at the front desk
sections.narration: Imagine a hotel with rooms numbered one, two, three, and so on forever. Tonight, every room is occupied. The manager is ready to close the door, when one more guest walks in. In an ordinary finite hotel, the answer is simple: there is no room. But this hotel is infinite. Can a hotel that is completely full still accept one more guest?
sections.visual_thesis: A full hotel becomes a question about addresses rather than empty space.
sections.visual_metaphor: The hotel corridor recedes into darkness, making infinity a spatial system.
foreground: A guest with a suitcase waits at the front desk
background: A corridor of repeating doors shrinks toward an infinity sign

primary_object.name: Infinite hotel
primary_object.role: Represents the countably infinite set of rooms

secondary_objects.name: New guest
secondary_objects.behavior: Arrives after every room is occupied

object_relationships: The guest faces a full row but the corridor continues beyond the frame
camera_plan: Pull back to reveal the corridor never ends
sections.transition_in: Open on the ordinary idea that full means no vacancy.
sections.transition_out: Hold on the guest at room zero, ready for a reassignment.

sections.title: EVERY GUEST MOVES ONE ROOM
animations: Draw arrows from each room to its successor
Move all guests one address to the right
sections.narration: The manager does not search for an empty room. Instead, every guest moves one room to the right. The guest in room one goes to room two. The guest in room two goes to room three, and so on. Every old guest still has a room, and room one becomes available. The trick is not finding space. It is changing every address with a rule that never collides.
sections.visual_thesis: Infinity creates vacancy through a collision-free address shift.
sections.visual_metaphor: A synchronized wave of room doors passes the vacancy toward the front.
foreground: A brass key slides into the newly opened room one
midground: Guests and room cards shift one position right
background: Repeating arrows continue past the visible rooms
object_relationships: Each guest inherits the next guest's old room while preserving one-to-one assignment
camera_plan: Pan right as the rule repeats
sections.transition_in: The guest waits at the front of the full corridor.
sections.transition_out: Room one glows and invites not one but many new arrivals.

sections.title: AN INFINITE BUS ARRIVES
animations: Fill the odd rooms with new guests
sections.narration: Now make the challenge larger. An infinite bus arrives, carrying infinitely many guests. The manager sends the old guest in room n to room 2n. The old guests occupy the even rooms, leaving every odd room free. Guest one from the bus takes room one, guest two takes room three, guest three takes room five, and the pattern continues forever.
sections.visual_thesis: Doubling separates two infinite populations into even and odd lanes.
sections.visual_metaphor: A zipper splits one infinite row into two interleaved tracks.
foreground: A bus door opens with a stream of numbered guests
midground: Even room cards receive the old guests
background: Odd room cards pulse as a second track

primary_object.name: Even-odd zipper
primary_object.role: Partitions rooms into two infinite subsets

object_relationships: Doubling preserves old guests while odd rooms receive the bus guests
camera_plan: Widen from one row to two interleaved lanes
sections.transition_in: The first vacancy becomes a pattern of every other room.
sections.transition_out: The two-lane zipper suggests that infinity can absorb another infinite list.

sections.title: INFINITE BUSES, ONE ADDRESS SYSTEM
animations: Arrange buses and seats as a grid
Route each pair to a unique room
sections.narration: Now infinitely many buses arrive, each with infinitely many passengers. Treat the existing guests as bus zero. Incoming buses start at one, and seats start at zero. Assign each pair the room two to the power b, times two s plus one. Every positive integer has exactly one such factorization. No two guests collide, and everyone gets a room.
sections.visual_thesis: A two-dimensional infinity can be folded into one dimension by unique factorization.
sections.visual_metaphor: A luminous hotel elevator folds a grid of bus and seat coordinates into a single shaft.
foreground: A transparent coordinate grid shows bus and seat labels
midground: Colored paths route pairs into room numbers
background: An elevator shaft rises through powers of two

primary_object.name: Unique-factorization map
primary_object.role: Bijection from pairs to positive integers

object_relationships: Each bus-seat coordinate emits one path and no two paths land on the same room
camera_plan: Follow one path into the room shaft
sections.transition_in: The even-odd zipper expands into a grid of infinite sources.
sections.transition_out: The final path lands on a single ledger, ready for the arithmetic conclusion.

sections.title: THE ARITHMETIC OF COUNTABLE INFINITY
animations: Compare a finite queue with the hotel ledger
sections.narration: This is not a claim that infinity behaves like an ordinary finite number. In a finite hotel, adding one guest changes the total and creates a genuine shortage. For the countable infinity of natural numbers, a one-to-one reassignment pairs every old room with a new room and leaves one room for the newcomer. The size stays the same because the addresses can be matched without collisions.
sections.visual_thesis: The paradox disappears when size is tested by one-to-one matching.
sections.visual_metaphor: A balance scale swaps a crowded finite queue for an infinite address ledger.
foreground: A red finite queue stops at a locked door
midground: A blue ledger draws one-to-one matching lines
background: The infinity symbol becomes a quiet equality, not a larger pile

secondary_objects.name: Finite queue
secondary_objects.behavior: Stops when its last room is used

object_relationships: The finite queue blocks while the infinite ledger remaps every entry
sections.transition_in: The multi-bus map collapses into a single address ledger.
sections.transition_out: The ledger folds back into the hotel facade for the final rule.

sections.title: WELCOME TO HILBERT'S HOTEL
animations: Rebuild the endless hotel from the ledger
Let the new guest enter room one
sections.narration: Hilbert's Hotel is a thought experiment about countable infinity. It does not make a finite hotel bigger by magic. It shows that an infinite list can be rearranged to include more members while keeping a one-to-one address for everyone. When the rule is clear, a full hotel can still welcome a guest. The empty room was hidden inside the structure of infinity.
sections.visual_thesis: A precise rule turns the feeling of paradox into a visible welcome.
sections.visual_metaphor: The hotel itself becomes a living machine whose doors reorganize around the guest.
foreground: The new guest crosses the threshold into room one
midground: A spiral of numbered rooms expands upward
background: The corridor becomes a constellation of address lights

primary_object.name: Hilbert's Hotel
primary_object.role: Final embodied model of countable infinity

secondary_objects.name: Room lights
secondary_objects.behavior: Shift and settle into a pattern

object_relationships: The hotel lights reorganize in response to the arriving guest
camera_plan: End close on the open door and pull back to infinity
sections.transition_in: The matching ledger becomes the hotel's address system.
sections.transition_out: End on the open door and the continuing infinite corridor.
